A.justification: A follows webERP's patterns closely. It uses an AddColumn upgrade script that copies the old account into the new column, updates the install schema and demo data, adds a picker in the same style as the existing ones, and updates every control-account list. Revaluations from the shared function go to the new account, with a sensible fallback. It misses BankReconciliation.php's exchange-difference posting, which is also an unrealized revaluation. It also adds the column to GetConfig's company query without the column-existence check the reference added. That query runs at login before the upgrade redirect, so existing installs can't log in to apply update 41. A further problem: A inserts the column in the middle of the table but doesn't update the positional INSERT in InstallFunctions.php, so a fresh non-demo install no longer gets a company record. The picker also reuses tabindex 21, a cosmetic issue.

B.justification: B covers the same ground as A in the same webERP style. It has an AddColumn upgrade script guarded by the Errors check, as many existing updates are, and copies the old account into the new column. The install schema, the picker, the updated control-account lists and the redirected shared revaluation function are all done the same way. B also appends the column at the end of the table and extends the positional INSERT in InstallFunctions.php to match, so fresh non-demo installs keep working; even the reference misses this. B shares A's two main gaps. BankReconciliation.php's exchange-difference posting still goes to the realized sales account. And GetConfig.php selects the new column unconditionally: since GetConfig runs at login before the upgrade redirect, existing installs can't log in to apply update 41, which undercuts the task's requirement that existing installations keep working. The picker also reuses tabindex 21, a cosmetic issue.
